extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (applicants, investigators, institutional administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of NIH extramural news items and short guidance updates about policies, application formats, review process changes, and resources relevant to preparing and submitting NIH grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the right models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: “NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scientifically sound models that are appropriate to the research question; favor approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. The emphasis is on fit-to-question rather than mandating specific model types.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: “Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified PF5 application format exactly and be aware that applications may be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time. Review the NIH overview video/resource to understand key features and procedural implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare DMS plans using the new 2026 pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH. Consult the issued format to ensure compliance with the required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations (Gold Standard Science plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic … NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applications and awards address replication and reproducibility where appropriate; consider including plans or approaches that promote reliability (e.g., replication strategies, rigorous design, transparent methods). Be aware of a new highlighted topic and initiatives that may affect review emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review status
rubrics_metrics.description: “My Application Was Scored as ‘Competitive But Not Discussed’ During Review. What Does This Mean? … Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that NIH implemented emergency modifications resulting in a cutoff that can leave strong applications in a middle third category labeled 'competitive but not discussed.' This explains a particular review outcome and its relation to percentiles/cutoffs; applicants should interpret such scores in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of peer review to CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: “One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency … In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) … we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that peer review processes have been consolidated under CSR; this may change logistical and procedural aspects of review (e.g., assignment, timelines, study sections). Applicants should monitor updates as centralization can affect submission-to-review workflows and expectations.
